questions.q: In Metrics Explorer, what does the aggregation setting control?
options: The retention period of the underlying data
Which Azure region the metric is collected from
Whether the metric is stored in Log Analytics
How a metric's data points are summarized over the chosen time range, such as Average vs. Maximum
questions.explain: The same CPU data can look completely different depending on whether you view it as an Average, Maximum, Minimum, Sum, or Count.

questions.q: A VM's Percentage CPU metric looks fine on Average but is pegged near 100% on Maximum for long stretches. What does this suggest?
options: Averages are always more accurate than maximums
The VM may be undersized for its workload — real evidence worth revisiting the VM size over
The metric data is corrupted and should be ignored
The VM has no CPU metric being collected
questions.explain: Switching to Maximum reveals sustained high-CPU periods that an average can hide — a concrete signal to reconsider VM sizing.

questions.q: Which Azure CLI command retrieves the same Percentage CPU data shown in Metrics Explorer?
options: az account show
az vm show --resource-group <rg> --name <vm>
az monitor metrics list --resource <vm-resource-id> --metric "Percentage CPU" --interval PT1H
az monitor log-analytics query
questions.explain: az monitor metrics list pulls the same metric data the portal's Metrics Explorer displays, useful for scripting a health check.
